title: Hindu widows
html_source: Sati (Sanskrit: satī, also spelled suttee) was an archaic Indian funeral custom where a widow immolated herself on her husband’s pyre, or committed suicide in another fashion shortly after her husband’s death. The practice was particularly prevalent among some Hindu communities. The practice was initially legalized by the colonial British officials specifying conditions when sati was allowed; then the practice was outlawed in 1829 in their territories in India.
